title: Atom-pair and torsion fingerprint Tanimoto GP
spec: In fit_predict, build a second hashed fingerprint per molecule with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048) and, separately, GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048), using GetFingerprintAsNumPy as bit vectors. Keep the existing Morgan-bit Tanimoto GP as the fingerprint member but replace its kernel with the Tanimoto kernel of the atom-pair bits, leaving choose_sigma2, gp_mean and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged. Only the kernel input changes. Do not add a new model.

title: Parent-fragment standardization before featurization
spec: Add a helper std_smiles(s) that parses the SMILES with RDKit, keeps the largest fragment via rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser, neutralizes charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and returns Chem.MolToSmiles of the result, falling back to the original string if parsing fails. Apply it to train_smiles and test_smiles at the top of fit_predict, so that desc_features, bit_fingerprints and MurckoScaffold all see the standardized molecules. Keep the rest of the pipeline the same.

title: Inner-CV selection of Morgan radius and bit size for the GP
spec: Inside fit_predict, build Morgan bit fingerprints for radius in {1, 2, 3} and fpSize in {1024, 2048}. For each of the six combinations, score the GP with choose_sigma2's grouped 5-fold procedure on the training molecules only, using Spearman as the score, and keep the best (radius, size, sigma2) triple for the final GP fit on all training molecules. The test set is never used for the choice. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend as they are.

title: Residual GP on out-of-fold descriptor LightGBM predictions
spec: Replace the rank blend with a residual scheme. Fit the descriptor LightGBM with 5-fold GroupKFold on the training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold, to get out-of-fold predictions. Compute residuals r = y_rank minus the out-of-fold prediction. Fit the Tanimoto GP (chosen sigma2) on r, using the Morgan bits. For test molecules, the output is the LightGBM prediction from a model fit on all training data plus the GP mean of the residuals, and this sum is then rank-transformed.

title: Pseudo-labelling of test molecules for the GP
spec: After the first GP prediction on test_smiles, take the test molecules whose predicted ranks are most confident, meaning the top 20% and bottom 20% by absolute distance from the median rank. Add them to the training set with their blended predictions as pseudo targets. Refit the Tanimoto GP on the augmented set with the same sigma2 and predict all test molecules again. The final output is the rank blend of the descriptor LightGBM and this second GP. Use only the seed argument for randomness.

title: Third blend member: Tanimoto kNN regression
spec: Add a k-nearest-neighbour regressor on the Morgan bits with Tanimoto similarity. For each test molecule, take the k=10 most similar training molecules by tanimoto(X_te, X_tr), and use a similarity-weighted average of their rank targets, with weights sim**3. Rank-transform this prediction and blend it with the existing two members using equal thirds, where the rank-blend weights become 0.4 for descriptor LightGBM, 0.3 for GP and 0.3 for kNN. Do not change the GP or the LightGBM.

title: Seed-averaged, feature-bagged descriptor LightGBM
spec: Train the descriptor LightGBM five times inside fit_predict, using seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4. Each fit keeps all other settings the same, with colsample_bytree=0.5 and subsample=0.8. Average the five test predictions before ranking. This stabilises the descriptor member, which is the noisiest part of the blend, and uses only the seed argument.

title: Huber objective for descriptor LightGBM on the rank target
spec: Change the LightGBM objective from L2 to Huber, with objective='huber' and alpha=0.2, since the rank target is in [0,1]. Keep the rest of the hyperparameters the same (400 trees, lr 0.03, num_leaves 31). The GP member and the rank blend stay unchanged. This tests whether robust loss helps on the rank-transformed target, where the outliers are compressed.

title: Density-scaled heteroscedastic GP noise
spec: Replace the scalar sigma2 in gp_mean with a per-training-molecule noise vector. For each training molecule, compute its mean Tanimoto similarity to its 10 nearest training neighbours (excluding itself). Set noise_i = sigma2 * (1 + c * (1 - density_i)), with c in {0.5, 1.0} chosen by the same grouped inner CV as sigma2. Use np.diag of this vector in place of sigma2 * np.eye in the solve. Test-time predictions use the same formula.

title: Cosine learning-rate decay with snapshot averaging in LightGBM
spec: Train the descriptor LightGBM with a cosine-decayed learning rate. Use lgb.train with a learning_rate callback that goes from 0.05 to 0.001 over 400 rounds. Save predictions at rounds 200, 300 and 400 using num_iteration, and average these three predictions before ranking. Keep num_leaves 31, subsample 0.8 and colsample 0.5 as they are. Seeds come from the seed argument.

title: Morgan radius/size sweep for GP
spec: In train.py, change the Tanimoto GP Morgan fingerprint settings N_BITS and RADIUS. Try RADIUS=3 and N_BITS=4096 (one change: set RADIUS=3, N_BITS=4096). The descriptor LightGBM is unaffected, since it does not use these settings. Keep everything else the same.

title: Atom-pair count Tanimoto GP kernel
spec: Replace the Morgan bit fingerprint in the GP with a hashed atom-pair fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize=2048, binary via GetFingerprintAsNumPy). Keep tanimoto, choose_sigma2 and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged.

title: Type-II ML GP noise and amplitude
spec: Replace the 3-value grid in choose_sigma2 with a finer grid of sigma2 in (0.03,0.06,0.1,0.2,0.3,0.5,1.0) and also a kernel amplitude scale chosen from (0.5,1,2) by the same grouped CV Spearman. Then pick the best pair. Keep the rest unchanged.

title: Multi-seed LightGBM averaging
spec: Train the descriptor LightGBM with 5 different seeds (seed+i) with subsample and colsample randomness, and average the predictions before rank blending. Reduces variance of the descriptor model.

title: Gaussian-rank target transform
spec: Replace the target y = rank/n with a normal score: scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(y)-0.5)/n). Use it for both LightGBM and GP fits. The final outputs are still rank-blended.

title: Residual GP on LightGBM out-of-fold predictions
spec: Compute 5-fold scaffold-grouped out-of-fold LightGBM descriptor predictions on the training set. Fit the Tanimoto GP to the residuals y - oof. Final score is the LightGBM test prediction plus the GP residual prediction, rank-averaged with the existing GP prediction at weight 0.5 versus the current blend. Keep the code compact.

title: Product kernel Tanimoto times descriptor RBF
spec: Build a kernel K = Tanimoto(Morgan bits) * exp(-gamma * ||z_i - z_j||^2/d) where z are the quantile-clipped, standardized RDKit descriptors of the top 30 by LightGBM importance (or all, clipped to ±5), gamma=0.5. Use it in the GP in place of the pure Tanimoto kernel. Keep the sigma2 selection.

title: Sigma2 ensemble of GP posteriors
spec: Instead of selecting a single sigma2, average the GP predictions from sigma2 in (0.1,0.3,1.0) with equal weights, removing the CV selection (faster, less noisy). Then rank-blend as before.

title: LightGBM on descriptors plus GP OOF prediction feature
spec: Compute grouped-CV out-of-fold Tanimoto GP predictions on the training set as one extra feature for the descriptor LightGBM. For test molecules use the full-train GP prediction as that feature. Then use the LightGBM output alone blended with the GP at the existing weights.

title: Huber objective for descriptor LightGBM
spec: Set objective='huber' with alpha=0.2 in the LGBMRegressor, since the rank target lies in [0,1]. Everything else is unchanged.

title: Morgan radius and bit-size sweep for the Tanimoto GP
spec: In train.py the Tanimoto-kernel GP uses Morgan bit fingerprints with RADIUS=2 and N_BITS=2048 (see bit_fingerprints). Replace this single fingerprint with an inner-CV choice over a small grid of fingerprint settings: (radius, fpSize) in {(2,2048), (3,2048), (3,4096), (2,1024)}. Generalize bit_fingerprints to take radius and fpSize arguments, and inside fit_predict compute the training Tanimoto kernel for each setting, score it with the same scaffold-grouped 5-fold GroupKFold Spearman loop already used in choose_sigma2 (reuse that code path, with sigma2 fixed at 0.3 during the fingerprint search), then keep the best setting and run the existing choose_sigma2 plus gp_mean on it. Keep the final 0.6/0.4 rank blend with the descriptor LightGBM unchanged. Cache fingerprints per (smiles, radius, fpSize) in a module-level dict so the 15 fits stay inside the 10-minute budget.

title: Gaussian-rank (normal score) target transform
spec: fit_predict currently maps the target to uniform ranks with y = rankdata(train_y)/len(train_y). Replace this with a Gaussian-rank (normal score) transform: y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(train_y) - 0.5) / len(train_y)). This leaves the ordering identical but spreads the tails, which changes what the squared-error objectives of both the descriptor LightGBM and the Tanimoto GP optimize (the GP prior mean subtraction in gp_mean also becomes better centred). Change nothing else: both models still see the same y, and the final output stays the 0.6/0.4 rank average of the two model predictions, so the transform only affects fitting, not the reported scale.

title: Average GP posteriors over a sigma2 grid instead of selecting one
spec: choose_sigma2 currently picks a single noise level from {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by scaffold-grouped CV Spearman and that one value is used in gp_mean. Selecting on ~970 molecules with a noisy criterion is unstable, so instead delete the selection and average: compute p_fp as the mean of the rank-normalized GP posterior means over the whole grid, i.e. for each s2 in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0} call gp_mean(K_tr, y, K_te, s2), convert each prediction vector to ranks divided by n, and average the four rank vectors. This is a cheap Bayesian-model-average over the noise hyperparameter: it needs one extra linear solve per s2 and removes an inner CV loop, so the job gets faster. Keep choose_sigma2 removed (or unused) and keep the final 0.6/0.4 blend with the descriptor LightGBM unchanged.

title: Third blend member: atom-pair plus torsion Tanimoto GP
spec: train.py blends a descriptor LightGBM (weight 0.6) with a Morgan-bit Tanimoto GP (weight 0.4). Add a third member that reuses the same GP machinery but a structurally different fingerprint: hashed atom-pair bits (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048)) concatenated with topological-torsion bits (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048)) into one 4096-bit binary vector. Build its Tanimoto kernel with the existing tanimoto function, reuse choose_sigma2 and gp_mean exactly as for the Morgan GP, and make the final prediction the rank average with weights 0.5 for the descriptor LightGBM, 0.25 for the Morgan GP and 0.25 for the new atom-pair/torsion GP (fixed weights, no search). Atom pairs and torsions encode topological distance rather than local environments, so the new member should decorrelate from the Morgan GP.

title: Seed-averaged models for variance reduction
spec: Each of the 15 harness fits currently trains one LightGBM on descriptors with random_state=seed, and the GP is deterministic. Reduce prediction variance by averaging the descriptor model over 5 seeds: fit lgb.LGBMRegressor with identical hyperparameters but random_state = seed + k for k in range(5) (subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.5 make each fit genuinely different), rank-normalize each model's test prediction, and average the five rank vectors to form p_desc. Also drop n_estimators to 300 if the runtime grows uncomfortable; the current single-model job is fast (well under the 10-minute cap for 15 fits), so 5 fits should still fit. Keep the GP branch and the 0.6/0.4 final rank blend unchanged.

title: Transductive smoothing of test predictions over test-test similarity
spec: After the final blended rank vector is computed in fit_predict, smooth it over the test-test chemical similarity graph. Compute the Morgan-bit Tanimoto similarity matrix S between the test molecules with the existing bit_fingerprints and tanimoto helpers, zero its diagonal, and for each test molecule keep only its 5 largest similarities (set the rest of the row to 0). Then return 0.8 * p + 0.2 * (S_knn @ p) / max(S_knn.sum(1), 1e-9), i.e. a single step of neighbour averaging with weights proportional to similarity, applied to the blended rank prediction p. This uses only test SMILES (allowed, they are given to fit_predict) and enforces that near-identical test molecules get near-identical predictions, which can only help a rank metric if the similarity graph is informative. Re-rank the result before returning.

title: Residual Tanimoto GP on top of the descriptor LightGBM
spec: Replace the parallel rank blend with a sequential (boosted) composition. First fit the descriptor LightGBM on the rank target y exactly as now and obtain its out-of-fold training predictions using scaffold-grouped 5-fold GroupKFold (groups from MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, as in choose_sigma2) so the residuals are honest. Then fit the Tanimoto-kernel GP (same bit_fingerprints, tanimoto, choose_sigma2, gp_mean) to the residual r = y - oof_pred instead of to y. The final prediction is the full-data LightGBM test prediction plus the GP residual prediction, returned as ranks divided by n. This lets the fingerprint model model only what the descriptors miss, instead of competing with them under a fixed 0.6/0.4 weight. Keep W_DESC unused or remove it.

title: Product kernel of Tanimoto and descriptor RBF for the GP
spec: The GP kernel in train.py is a plain Morgan-bit Tanimoto similarity. Multiply it by a smooth descriptor kernel so that molecules must be similar both structurally and in physicochemical space. Build Z from a small, stable descriptor subset (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHAcceptors, NumHDonors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, RingCount), standardize it with the training mean and sd, clip to [-5, 5], and form R = exp(-gamma * squared euclidean distance / d) with gamma chosen from {0.25, 1.0} by the same scaffold-grouped CV Spearman loop already used in choose_sigma2. The GP kernel becomes K = K_tanimoto * (0.5 + 0.5 * R) (so the descriptor term modulates rather than dominates). Keep choose_sigma2, gp_mean and the 0.6/0.4 final rank blend otherwise unchanged.

title: Shift the blend weight toward the fingerprint GP
spec: W_DESC = 0.6 in train.py was chosen when the fingerprint member was an ExtraTrees model; the member has since been replaced by the stronger Tanimoto-kernel GP, so the fixed weight is likely stale. Make a one-line change setting W_DESC = 0.45, i.e. the descriptor LightGBM rank gets 0.45 and the GP rank gets 0.55. Change nothing else. This is deliberately a single-constant probe (no inner search, which has already been tried and cost accuracy); if it moves the loss by more than the ~0.007 noise sd it identifies the direction the weight should go, and if not the simple 0.6 stays.

title: Snapshot ensemble over LightGBM boosting rounds
spec: The descriptor LightGBM runs 400 trees at learning_rate 0.03 and only its final iteration is used, so the prediction sits at whatever point 400 rounds happens to land on. Replace the single prediction with a snapshot average: fit the model once as now, then call lgbm.predict(X_test, num_iteration=k) for k in {200, 275, 350, 400}, rank-normalize each of the four prediction vectors, and average them to form p_desc. This costs no extra training time (predictions at truncated iteration counts come from the same fitted booster) and acts as an implicit regularizer against over- or under-shooting the optimal number of rounds on only ~780 training molecules per fold. Keep the GP branch and the 0.6/0.4 final blend unchanged.

title: Average GP posteriors over a sigma2 grid instead of selecting one
spec: In the current train.py, fit_predict blends a descriptor LightGBM rank with a Tanimoto-kernel GP posterior mean on Morgan bits; the GP noise level is picked by choose_sigma2, which runs a 5-fold scaffold-grouped inner CV over sigma2 in {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} and returns the single best value. Selecting one value from three noisy inner-CV scores is unstable. Replace the selection with an average: delete choose_sigma2 (and its now-unused GroupKFold / MurckoScaffold / spearmanr imports if nothing else uses them) and instead compute the GP posterior mean for each sigma2 in a fixed grid of (0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0), rank-transform each resulting test prediction vector (rankdata / n), and average those ranks to form p_fp. Keep everything else identical, including the final 0.6/0.4 rank blend with the descriptor LightGBM. This removes the inner CV, so the job should also get faster.

title: Morgan radius and bit-size sweep for the Tanimoto GP
spec: train.py currently builds the GP kernel from a single Morgan bit fingerprint with RADIUS = 2 and N_BITS = 2048 (see bit_fingerprints and the module-level settings). These two numbers were never tuned. Make bit_fingerprints take radius and fpSize as arguments, then run one job per configuration is not possible, so instead average over fingerprint scales: build three bit fingerprint matrices, (radius 1, 2048 bits), (radius 2, 2048 bits) and (radius 3, 4096 bits), compute a Tanimoto kernel for each, and for each kernel run the existing choose_sigma2 plus gp_mean pipeline. Rank-transform the three test prediction vectors (rankdata / n) and average them with equal weight to form p_fp. Keep the descriptor LightGBM branch and the final 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged. If runtime becomes a concern, call choose_sigma2 only on the radius-2 kernel and reuse that sigma2 for the other two.

title: Add an atom-pair and topological-torsion Tanimoto GP as a third blend member
spec: train.py blends two ranks: a LightGBM on the full RDKit descriptor list (weight W_DESC = 0.6) and a Tanimoto-kernel GP on Morgan radius-2 bits (weight 0.4). Morgan captures local atom environments only; add a complementary topology view. Using rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048) and rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048), build the concatenated 4096-bit binary fingerprint (GetFingerprintAsNumPy) for train and test, form its Tanimoto kernel with the existing tanimoto helper, choose its noise with the existing choose_sigma2, and get a third posterior mean with gp_mean. Blend the three rank vectors with weights 0.5 for the descriptor LightGBM, 0.25 for the Morgan GP and 0.25 for the new atom-pair/torsion GP. Cache the generators at module level so they are built once.

title: Tanimoto GP on the residuals of the descriptor LightGBM
spec: Currently train.py trains a descriptor LightGBM and a Morgan-bit Tanimoto GP independently on the same rank target and then rank-averages their test predictions with weights 0.6/0.4. Replace this parallel blend with a boosted (sequential) form: first get out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set using a 5-fold scaffold-grouped split (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles as group key, GroupKFold, both already imported), compute the residual r = y_rank minus out-of-fold prediction, then fit the Tanimoto-kernel GP (same bit_fingerprints, tanimoto, choose_sigma2, gp_mean path, but on r instead of y) and predict residuals for the test molecules. Refit the LightGBM on all training data for the test prediction. The final score is rankdata(p_lgbm_full + p_resid_gp) / n. Keep model hyperparameters as they are.

title: Gaussian-rank (normal-score) target transform
spec: fit_predict in train.py currently transforms the target to uniform ranks with y = rankdata(train_y) / len(train_y) before fitting both the descriptor LightGBM and the Tanimoto GP. A uniform target has hard edges and heavy mass at the extremes, which is awkward for the squared-loss GP in particular. Replace it with the normal-score (van der Waerden) transform: y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(train_y) - 0.5) / len(train_y)), which maps the ranks to a standard-normal shape. Nothing else changes: the GP prior mean subtraction, choose_sigma2, the LightGBM fit and the final rank blend all work unchanged since the transform is strictly monotone and the output is rank-averaged anyway. This is a one-line change plus the norm import.

title: Transductive smoothing of test predictions over the test-test similarity graph
spec: train.py returns W_DESC * rankdata(p_desc)/n + (1 - W_DESC) * rankdata(p_fp)/n as its final prediction and never exploits the structure of the test set itself. Add a cheap transductive post-processing step: after forming the final blended score vector p, compute the Morgan-bit Tanimoto similarity matrix S among the test molecules (reuse bit_fingerprints and tanimoto on test_smiles only), zero its diagonal, keep for each test molecule only its 5 largest similarities (set the rest of the row to 0), row-normalize the kept weights, and return rankdata(0.8 * p + 0.2 * (W @ p)) / n where W is that sparse row-normalized matrix. The idea is that chemically near-identical test molecules should receive similar predictions, which denoises the ranking. Keep the weight 0.8/0.2 and k = 5 as fixed module-level constants so they are easy to see.

title: Average the descriptor LightGBM over several seeds
spec: In train.py the descriptor branch is a single LightGBM (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10) fit with random_state=seed. With subsampling and column sampling at 0.5, a single fit carries noticeable variance that directly enters the 0.6-weighted rank. Replace it with an average of five such models using random_state = seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4 (all other hyperparameters identical), rank-transform each model's test prediction, and average those five rank vectors to form p_desc. Keep n_jobs=8 and reduce per-model n_estimators only if the job exceeds about 7 minutes. The GP branch and the final 0.6/0.4 blend stay exactly as they are.

title: Product kernel of Tanimoto on fingerprints and RBF on descriptors
spec: The GP branch of train.py uses a pure Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits (tanimoto(X_tr, X_tr)), so it is blind to the physchem descriptors that the LightGBM branch sees. Enrich the kernel: compute an RBF kernel on a small set of standardized descriptors, and multiply it elementwise into the Tanimoto kernel. Concretely, take the descriptor matrix from desc_features, select a handful of interpretable columns by name (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHAcceptors, NumHDonors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3) by looking up their position in Descriptors.descList, standardize them using the training mean and std (guard zero std), and form K_rbf = exp(-gamma * squared euclidean distance) with gamma = 1 / n_selected_features. Use K = K_tanimoto * K_rbf everywhere the Tanimoto kernel is currently used (train-train for choose_sigma2 and gp_mean, test-train for the posterior mean). Keep the rest of the script, including the 0.6/0.4 rank blend, unchanged.

title: Local GP on the k most similar training molecules
spec: train.py fits one global Tanimoto-kernel GP on all ~780 training molecules per fold. Hepatocyte clearance structure-activity relationships are local, so add a local variant and average it in. For each test molecule, find its 150 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules (using the Morgan bit fingerprints already computed by bit_fingerprints and the tanimoto helper), solve the GP on that submatrix only (reuse gp_mean with the same sigma2 that choose_sigma2 returns for the global kernel) and take the posterior mean at that single test point. This costs about 780 small 150x150 solves per fold, which is fast with numpy. Rank-transform both the global and the local posterior means and average them 50/50 to form p_fp; keep the final 0.6/0.4 blend against the descriptor LightGBM unchanged.

title: Huber objective for the descriptor LightGBM
spec: The descriptor branch of train.py is a LightGBM regressor with the default L2 objective, fitted on the uniform rank target y = rankdata(train_y) / n. Since only the Spearman correlation of the output matters and the rank target is bounded in (0, 1], squared loss spends capacity on the extreme ranks. Change the LightGBM to objective='huber' with alpha=0.1 (about one tenth of the target range), keeping all other hyperparameters (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1) and the whole GP branch and 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged. This is a two-argument edit; if huber is clearly worse the same slot tells us the loss shape is not the bottleneck.
